docs.title: Fresh Orange Juice Vending Machine
docs.text:
An automation showcase at ASU: a machine that squeezes and serves fresh orange juice on demand, designed to comply with IEC 60335 household-appliance safety.

AutomationIEC 60335Food-contact designEmbedded control

Design focus Safety Source available on request

docs.title: Why it's hard
docs.text:
Automatic juice machines exist, but they are hard to run well. The juicer itself is the easy part. The hard parts are what surround it:

Challenge Why it matters Waste handling Peel is roughly half the fruit by weight and spoils within a day Food-contact hygiene Blades, chute and nozzle need cleaning that actually works Siting Power, refrigeration and a drain all in one place Input cost Several oranges per cup, with seasonal price swings

docs.title: Design focus
docs.text: The engineering that sets this machine apart is the self-sanitizing dispense path and a waste system that stretches the time between service visits, not the juicing mechanism.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text: The design follows IEC 60335, the international safety standard for household and similar electrical appliances: protection against electric shock, moving parts, heating and abnormal operation.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: In design. Mechanical layout, control architecture and safety analysis will be added here as they are completed.
